clue.text: What holidaymaker needs? Foreign bar and gossip

indicators.note: foreign means strange or unfamiliar, so the following words are turned into something new by reordering

explanation.surface: A tourist abroad hankers after a local bar and a good gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests holiday pleasures, a foreign bar and chat; 'Foreign' actually signals that the letters of BAR AND GOSSIP are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller flying on holiday must show this document at the gate before getting on the aircraft.

clue.text: Arrive wearing almost finest suits

indicators.note: something wearing clothes has them around it, so the word for arrive sits inside
almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: finest means best
to arrive is to come

explanation.surface: Someone turns up dressed in nearly their best outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing, but it is the verb, as in 'that hat really suits you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour that flatters you is said to become you, which is the same as saying it is right for you.

clue.text: A bit cut off

parts.note: a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A small piece has been snipped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something isolated or separated from others stands away from them, detached.

clue.text: Hanging criminal tended to captivate writer

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the anagram encloses the writer
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of tended are rearranged

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A villain looking after things charms an author, with a hint of the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: Beside 'criminal', 'Hanging' suggests an execution, but it simply means dangling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended from a support, like a pendant on a chain, hangs down from it.

clue.text: Twelve working after union oddly ignored

indicators.note: after means the word for working comes after the letters from union
the odd-placed letters of union are skipped, leaving its second and fourth

parts.note: union with its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters removed
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Twelve people are back at work once the union's odd demands are set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, so the number stands for that hour of the day.

clue.text: Burden? I'm leaving job

indicators.note: leaving means the letters of I'm go out of the longer word

parts.note: an imposition is a burden placed on someone
I'm gives the letters IM, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A worker complains that their role is a burden and resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: IMPOSITION loses IM, the letters of 'I'm' ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or appointment in an organisation is a job someone holds.

clue.text: Son married East European

parts.note: to have married is to have wed
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A son has married a woman from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'East European' as one phrase; 'East' gives E and 'European' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede comes from Sweden, a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Keep quiet about first shot at Wimbledon?

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft or quiet
re means about or concerning
each point in tennis begins with a serve; Wimbledon is the famous London tennis championship

explanation.surface: Spectators are told to hush just before a player serves at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Keep quiet' a request for silence; 'Keep' alone is the definition, and 'quiet' gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve or maintain something in its original state is to keep it.

clue.text: Sunglasses primarily suit very hot place

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of suit is taken

parts.note: Hades is the underworld, traditionally pictured as infernally hot

explanation.surface: Dark glasses are mainly what's needed for a scorching destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is the informal word for dark glasses worn against bright sun.

clue.text: Chimps with no bananas securing adult supporters

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the rearranged letters enclose the adult
bananas means crazy, so the letters of chimps and no are mixed up

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Apes without fruit are clinging to a grown-up and their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit the chimps lack, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion of a cause is someone who backs it, an advocate or defender.

clue.text: What traps craft? Solid ground

indicators.note: traps means catches and holds inside, so the word for what encloses the craft

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
craft means art or skill

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which vessel ensnares, then a mention of dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is soil or land, as opposed to sea or air, the firm surface underfoot.

clue.text: Expression of hesitation about very small insurrection

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the hesitation word is read backwards

parts.note: um is a sound people make when hesitating
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly mentions a minor uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is a rebellion, especially by sailors or soldiers against their officers.

clue.text: Harassed fools maybe returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, one example of desserts

explanation.surface: A frazzled person is being made a fool of again.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool here is the British pudding of fruit puree folded into cream, not a silly person; the 'maybe' marks it as one example of desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harassed is under pressure and anxious, which is to be strained or tense.

clue.text: Flipping short rubbish bags female put up with

indicators.note: bags means takes or holds, so the reversed word encloses the letter for female
flipping means turning over, so the shortened word is read backwards
short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: refuse is rubbish

explanation.surface: An exasperated person tolerated a woman's rubbish bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims REFUSE to REFUS, 'Flipping' turns it to SUFER, and 'bags' takes F into it. 'Flipping' passes as a mild curse and 'bags' as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or endure something unpleasant is to bear it, as in 'suffer fools gladly'.

clue.text: Passionately cry — I feel bad

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of cry I feel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A distressed person sobs that they feel awful.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something fiercely is to do it with intense feeling or vehemence.

clue.text: Relates worries about old politician

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for worries goes round the other letters

parts.note: cares are worries
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts their concerns about a former politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate one thing to another is to draw a connection or comparison between them.

clue.text: Let me pour out oil

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of let me pour are rearranged

explanation.surface: A polite offer to do the pouring of some oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pour out' reads as one phrase, but 'pour' belongs to the letters being mixed and 'out' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is crude oil, the fossil fuel extracted from underground.

clue.text: Many fish endlessly grabbing head

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the shortened fish encloses the word for head
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a mullet is a kind of fish
the tip is the head or top end of something

explanation.surface: A fish swallows the head of another, many of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a body part here but the tip or top end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiple describes having several or numerous parts, so it stands for numerous things.

clue.text: Singular thing axeman uses without large reach

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for large is removed

parts.note: an axeman is slang for a guitarist (an axe being a guitar), who strums with a plectrum
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A lone woodcutter's tool, minus something large, has a long reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axeman' suggests a woodcutter, but in rock slang an axe is an electric guitar, so his tool is the plectrum, or pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a range or scope, as in a wide spectrum of opinion, the full extent covered.

clue.text: Gets cracking pastry in ship

indicators.note: in places the pastry inside the letters for ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Someone breaks open a pie aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like breaking the pastry, but 'Gets cracking' is an idiom for beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cracking is an informal idiom for beginning something promptly.

clue.text: Strip and run naked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a narrow band or stripe, as of colour or light
second meaning: to dash about unclothed in public

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' reads as undressing, which leads straight into running naked, but it is a separate noun sense: a thin line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a long thin mark and the act of dashing nude through a public place.

clue.text: Boat circling second tense river bird

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the boat word encloses the other letters

parts.note: the keel is the boat's backbone, standing in for the boat itself
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boat goes round once more on a tense river trip, watched by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A keel is the spine of a boat's hull, here standing for the whole boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon that hovers before swooping on its prey.

clue.text: Bang on a clapped-out car with copper inside

indicators.note: inside means the copper symbol goes within the word for the old car

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, worn-out vehicle
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A wrecked old car with a police officer in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clapped-out' looks like an anagram signal but, with 'car', is a definition of CRATE, British slang for an old banger. 'copper' is the metal, not the policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is British slang for exactly right, so it means correct or precise.

clue.text: King Lear, perhaps, in play orchestrated upset

definitions.note: a noun: King Lear is an example of a royal, a member of a royal family

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down clue the letters read upwards
in means the letters are contained within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters is found across these two words

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's king appears in a play that was staged in a disrupted way.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters LAYOR are found in 'play orchestrated'; 'upset' turns them over.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal is a member of a monarch's family, and Lear is a legendary British king.

clue.text: Dogs scratching soft heaps

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, so the letter for soft is crossed off

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Dogs are scratching at soft piles of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, as in oodles of money.

clue.text: Student had a meal right afterwards

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A student ate, quite properly, after everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, coming after the present moment.

clue.text: Zoom half cut off the French novelist

indicators.note: half cut off means the second half of the word is lost, keeping its first half

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A camera zoom shot partly cropped, featuring a French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was a nineteenth-century French writer of fiction, author of Germinal.

clue.text: On this we watched Kojak?

parts.note: Kojak was a 1970s American TV police drama; its star's first name is also the informal British word for the set it was watched on

explanation.walkthrough: The informal British word for a television is also the first name of Kojak's star, Telly Savalas, which makes the question mark's double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewers watched the detective series on a television set, the screen in the living room.

clue.text: One who demonstrates in favour of examiner

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a tester is someone who examines or checks

explanation.surface: Someone shows how in support of an examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demonstrates' suggests showing how something works, but here it means marching in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A person at a rally or march voicing objection is said to demonstrate.

clue.text: I felt alarmed at sea?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seasick or nervous person admits to panic on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a wry picture of the top naval commander confessing fright on the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest rank in a navy commands a fleet, so it could be the speaker of these words on the ocean.
